evals.prompt: We run a marketplace and have a moderation queue for new listings. Right now a GPT prompt returns JSON like {"prohibited": true, "reason": "..."} and we act on it. It's slow (2-3s), costs add up at 40k listings/day, and it flip-flops on borderline items. Someone mentioned Jev / TypeSafe. Should we use it? If so how would you set it up, and what should stay on the LLM?
evals.expected_output: A clear verdict (fit, with the generation of 'reason' text staying on an LLM or dropped), a decomposed question bundle (several Nouls for specific prohibited categories, a Score for condition/severity or a Choice with a none option), an explicit threshold policy with a review band, an evaluation plan with labelled listings and adversarial checks, and a note about pinning the model version. Should not propose Jev writing the reason text. Should mention keeping deterministic checks (price sanity, banned-word lists) in code.

evals.prompt: Can I point Cursor / my coding agent at jev-latest instead of Claude so it's faster and cheaper? And separately, would Jev be good for parsing dates out of our contract PDFs and telling us which contract expires first?
evals.expected_output: Explains plainly that Jev cannot replace the LLM behind a coding agent (no generation, no tool loop) and redirects to where it fits inside one (gating tool calls, judging outputs). For the dates: PDFs must be OCR'd to text first; Jev should read date parts as Choices with none/out_of_range options and code should assemble dates and do the comparison; the comparison itself is not a Jev job. Should not invent request fields.

evals.prompt: Here is our RAG pipeline: user question -> embedding search returns top 20 chunks -> we stuff all 20 into the LLM prompt -> answer. Users complain about hallucinated answers when the docs don't actually cover the question. Review this and tell me where, if anywhere, a decision model like Jev would help, and what I'd have to change.
evals.expected_output: An applicability table or equivalent: a per-chunk relevance question (Noul or Score) to filter/rerank before the LLM; a 'does the retrieved material contain an answer at all' Noul so the system can decline; a post-answer verification Choice (supported / unsupported / declined) with a review or retry path. Specifies what stays in code (top-k, thresholds, decline behaviour), warns about state size / context rot when batching chunks, and recommends evaluating on labelled questions before setting thresholds. Vendor-neutral on how to call it.
